newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ENGLAND'S MILLWALL FACE CASH CRISIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLAND'S MILLWALL FACE CASH CRISIS.

text.p: The owners of English second division soccer club Millwall called in administrators on Tuesday to help the London team weather a financial crisis.
Trading in Millwall Holdings Plc shares on the London Stock Exchange had been suspended earlier on Tuesday pending a statement on the company's financial position.
Chairman Peter Mead then announced that the company had appointed an administrator to run the company while it tried to arrange fresh financing.
Millwall were one of the first English soccer teams to join the stock market, a move which a growing number of clubs have followed in recent years.

Millwall shares were issued at a price of 20p in 1989 when the club was enjoying its only taste of life in the top flight of English soccer. The club have been relegated twice since and the shares are now worth just 4p each.
Mead told Reuters that the company was seeking a "once and for all solution" to its financial problems rather than having to sell off its best players as in the past.

"The essential thing is to break out of the vicious circle," he said. When asked whether Millwall would have to sell players in the short-term to tide it over its shortfall, Mead said: "I don't know. That is why (administrator) David Buckler is here."
Mead would not reveal Millwall's debt level but it is thought to be just under 7.5 million pounds ($12.46 million).
He said that the club would reveal more of its refinancing plans on Wednesday but added that there had been a very encouraging initial response in talks on Tuesday.
Mead reported interest in a rights issue and said that there were other potential investors who might support the company.

Millwall have sold off players such as U.S. goalkeeper Kasey Keller, defender Ben Thatcher and midfielder Alex Rae to premier league clubs since relegation at the end of last season. The team are currently among the front-runners in the second division. ($1=.6021 Pound)
